about.title: Clayton Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: Clayton's mix of small businesses, contractors, and workers commuting along Clayton Road and Marsh Creek Road means job-related injuries here can range from warehouse falls to vehicle collisions during work duties. Under California law, workers' compensation is generally your only path against your own employer, no matter who caused the accident — but that's not always the full picture. If a subcontractor, equipment manufacturer, property owner, or another driver contributed to your injury, you may have a separate claim outside the workers' comp system. Given Clayton's proximity to busier corridors like Oakhurst Drive and Keller Ridge Drive, work-related vehicle incidents aren't unusual. Our team reviews workplace injury claims directly and can help you understand the details, explain your options, and determine whether a third-party claim might apply alongside your workers' comp benefits.
commonInjuries: Falls from ladders, scaffolding, or uneven surfaces
Vehicle collisions while driving for work
Injuries from defective tools or safety gear

items.title: Understanding the Exclusive Remedy Rule
items.desc: California generally limits your claim against your own employer to workers' compensation, regardless of fault. We can help you determine whether that's truly your only path here.

items.title: Spotting Third-Party Liability
items.desc: If a subcontractor, property owner, or equipment maker played a role in your injury, you may have a separate claim outside workers' comp. That claim carries its own two-year deadline, so timing matters.

items.title: Protection Against Retaliation
items.desc: Reporting an injury to your employer within 30 days is required, and retaliation for doing so is illegal in California. We can help you understand your rights if you're worried about pushback at work.

items.question: I was hurt on a job site along Clayton Road — can I file a claim against my employer directly?
items.answer: In most cases, California workers' compensation is your exclusive remedy against your own employer, even if the injury happened on a busy stretch like Clayton Road. However, if another party — such as a subcontractor or equipment supplier — contributed to the accident, you might have a separate third-party claim. We can review the specifics and explain which path applies to your situation.

items.question: What if my injury happened while driving for work near Marsh Creek Road or Oakhurst Drive?
items.answer: Work-related vehicle incidents can involve both workers' compensation and a potential third-party claim, especially if another driver was involved. Since another driver isn't your employer, a separate injury claim against them may be possible in addition to any workers' comp benefits. Getting the timeline and facts sorted out early helps preserve your options.

items.question: How long do I have to report my injury or file a claim?
items.answer: You generally need to report a workplace injury to your employer within 30 days to protect your workers' compensation rights. If a third party's negligence contributed to your injury, that separate claim typically carries a two-year deadline. Because these timelines differ, it helps to talk with us sooner rather than later.
